# ALS evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Proposed answer (the answer to evaluate):
CDK5 phosphorylation of Nup98 initiates nuclear-pore barrier failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy models of ALS

Hypothesis. In human iPSC-derived spinal motor neurons with doxycycline-inducible TDP-43 lacking a functional nuclear-localization signal, CDK5 phosphorylation of Nup98 is the proposed initiating, pore-intrinsic cause of selective transport failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy relevant to ALS and ALS/FTD with cytoplasmic TDP-43. Downstream responses are impaired NLS import, reduced NES export, increased size-step passive leak, loss of nuclear TDP-43, growth of cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies, and later neuronal dysfunction. The CDK5–Nup98 step is an uncited assumption.

Supported premises. Nuclear-pore and transport components associate with insoluble TDP-43, and disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in cell systems, with related pore pathology in ALS tissue [S1]. The initiating event and cross-subtype generality remain open [S1]. Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA is linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import, and transport or repeat-RNA manipulations modify model phenotypes [S2]. This route is specific to C9orf72 [S2]. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form independently of conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport proteins, and accompany import failure, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death; phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulates in those assemblies [S3]. Cellular stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs transport, and changing stress-granule assembly modifies those defects [S4]. Premises cite PMIDs 29311743 [S1], 26308891 [S2], 30853299 [S3], and 29628143 [S4].

Speculative bridges. Unverified prior knowledge, outside this packet and without a citation identifier, holds that Nup98 is an FG-nucleoporin whose phosphorylation can relax pore selectivity and that CDK5 is a proline-directed kinase in post-mitotic neurons. CDK5 is the single pre-registered kinase. An NPC-fraction phosphoproteomic gate locks residues: a site enters the allele list only when CDK5 deletion lowers its occupancy by ≥50% and the peptide maps to Nup98. S/T-to-A and S/T-to-D alleles use only that list. The assumed order is CDK5 activation, Nup98 phosphorylation, NPC barrier change, then transport-factor build-up in stress granules or in separate TDP-43 assemblies, then loss of nuclear TDP-43 [S3]. C9orf72-ALS keeps RanGAP mislocalization as a separate entry [S2].

Alternative explanations. Transport receptors and Ran regulators can be sequestered in stress granules [S4] or in stress-granule-independent TDP-43 assemblies [S3] with nucleoporins left unmodified. Nucleoporin mislocalization can follow binding to insoluble TDP-43 [S1]. Broad stress can degrade transport in the absence of Nup98 phosphorylation. Repeat RNA and RanGAP pathology can explain C9orf72 transport failure [S2].

Discriminating preclinical test. Primary samples are TDP-43 motor neurons at 0, 6, 12, 24, 48, and 72 hours after induction. A C9orf72 repeat culture is a context comparator. NPC mass spectrometry and phospho-blot quantify locked-site occupancy. An NLS reporter and endogenous TDP-43 score import; an NES reporter scores export; passive probes near 20 kDa and 70 kDa score size-step leak. G3BP1 granules, G3BP1-negative TDP-43 assemblies, and NPC-resident Nup98 are scored as separate compartments. Initiation requires a ≥2-fold occupancy rise at least one 6-hour interval before a ≥30% fall in the NLS nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio versus uninduced wells. Necessity is tested on this TDP-43 time course alone: once S/T-to-A Nup98 reaches ≥70% of NPC Nup98 signal, the ≥30% import drop is absent through 72 hours. Import is interpreted only after that incorporation threshold is met. After stress-granule induction [S4], granule blockade returns wild-type Nup98 import to within 10% of the unstressed baseline. After ≥70% NPC incorporation, S/T-to-D Nup98 leaves a residual ≥30% import defect after the same blockade. TDP-43 de-mixing blockade [S3] uses the same thresholds in the assembly compartment.

Falsifying observation. Reject initiation if a ≥30% NLS-import drop and nuclear TDP-43 loss occur while locked-site occupancy stays below 2-fold at every sample. Reject the CDK5 assignment if no Nup98 site falls ≥50% after CDK5 deletion. Reject necessity if incorporated S/T-to-A Nup98 leaves onset and the ≥30% drop unchanged while granule or assembly blockade restores import. Reject sufficiency if S/T-to-D Nup98 impairs import only when transport factors are sequestered, or if granule blockade restores import to within 10% of baseline despite ≥70% phosphomimetic incorporation. A ≥2-fold phospho-Nup98 rise confined to the C9orf72 comparator, with a sub-2-fold change in the TDP-43 model, rejects this disease context.

Limitations. CDK5 and the residue list stay assumptions until the gate passes, and phosphorylation may mark later pore injury. Cultures omit glia, aging, and circuits. Partial Nup98 replacement can mask an effect. Phospho-reagents can cross-react with phosphorylated TDP-43 or other FG-nucleoporins. Preserved import still leaves other nucleoporins and the RanGAP axis [S2] open. Treatment validation lies outside this experiment.

Promisingness is 0.37, the mean of direct support for phospho-initiation (0.05), support for a TDP-43–transport link (0.75), separability from sequestration (0.40), and tractability of the gated allele test (0.28). Confidence is 0.48, the mean of premise-reading confidence (0.80), confidence in the CDK5 and site choice (0.20), and confidence that these thresholds can reject initiation (0.44).

Ranked proposal:
CDK5 phosphorylation of Nup98 initiates nuclear-pore barrier failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy models of ALS
